title: Incidence and risk factors for persistent postmastectomy pain (PPMP) in trans male patients
summary:
This study aims to identify potential persistent pain or sensory disturbances in the surgical area.
Our interest in conducting this study stems from the desire to identify potential persistent pain or sensory disturbances in the surgical area.
Although many current studies address the selection of appropriate surgical techniques and postoperative complications and their correlation with patient satisfaction, only a small number of published studies have evaluated persistent postoperative and sensory disturbances. This is an important question, however, as chronic pain can significantly impact quality of life.
The aim of this project is to determine the incidence of persistent post-mastectomy pain (PPMP) in female-to-male (FtM) patients. The primary endpoint is the occurrence of PPMP 6 months after the procedure.
Furthermore, a possible association between medical history, prior medication, and depressive symptoms and the occurrence of PPMP will be investigated in order to identify risk and protective factors for PPMP. Secondary endpoints include the correlation between the incidence of PPMP and the presence of underlying psychiatric or neurological disorders, as well as changes in depressive symptoms and surgical factors
conditions: persistent post-mastectomy pain (PPMP) in female-to-male (FtM) patients.

interventions.name: This is a prospective cohort study. The study will be conducted by the Department of Anesthesiology at the Florence Nightingale Hospital in Düsseldorf. Recruitment will take place in the pre-anesthesia clinic of the Department of Anesthesiology, Intensive Care Medicine, and Pain Therapy at the Flore

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients for female-to-male mastectomy between June 2025 and June 2026
- Adults capable of giving informed consent
- Written consent
- German language skills
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients with known chronic chest pain
- Breast surgery for other reasons (not gender reassignment surgery)
- Previous breast surgery
- Refusal to consent
